t: No part of any appropriation for the fiscal year 1948 contained in this or any other Act shall be paid to any person for the filling of any position for which he or she has been nominated after the Senate has voted not to approve of the nomination of said person.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a Senate vote on a nomination is a kind of consultation or approval process. But the Senate is part of Congress and so inside the federal government, and this provision only restricts the use of appropriations to pay rejected nominees. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted or given a right to challenge any federal decision.
fable.s: after the Senate has voted not to approve of the nomination of said person

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a funding restriction on the federal government regarding the payment of salaries for individuals whose nominations were rejected by the Senate. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside party (such as the public, states, or private entities) in making a decision. The interaction described is between the Executive branch (nominating/paying) and the Legislative branch (Senate voting), both of which are inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: No part of any appropriation for the fiscal year 1948 contained in this or any other Act shall be paid to any person for the filling of any position for which he or she has been nominated after the Senate has voted not to approve of the nomination of said person.

opus.w: This provision bars paying salaries to nominees the Senate has rejected. It is a limit on how appropriations may be spent. The only body involved besides the executive is the Senate, which is part of the federal government, so nothing crosses the federal boundary. No states, experts, members of the public or other outside parties take part in any federal decision.
opus.s: No part of any appropriation for the fiscal year 1948 contained in this or any other Act shall be paid to any person for the filling of any position for which he or she has been nominated after the Senate has voted not to approve of the nomination of said person.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The Senate voting on a nomination looks like an outside check on an executive decision. But the Senate is part of Congress, so it is inside the federal government. The section also just limits the use of appropriations. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a funding restriction based on the outcome of a Senate confirmation vote. The Senate is an internal component of the federal government, so its actions do not constitute participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for the executive branch to consult with states, the public, or other non-federal entities before making a decision.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation for the fiscal year 1948 contained in this or any other Act shall be paid to any person for the filling of any position for which he or she has been nominated after the Senate has voted not to approve of the nomination of said person.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Senate's vote is a form of participation because it involves a legislative body reviewing a nomination. However, the Senate is part of the federal government (inside the boundary), and the definition explicitly excludes interactions solely within the federal government. Furthermore, this section is a funding restriction based on a past event (the Senate vote), not a requirement for future consultation or coordination with outside parties.
